HereAreSomeThings.target: Here are some things you can do that may improve performance:

DYGLEFRTextureUploadLimited.target: Performance is limited by the cost of uploading textures to the GPU during the frame. Whenever possible upload all textures during initialization. If this is not possible, restrict the loading of textures to between frames.

DYGLEFRCPULimited.target: Performance is limited by the cost of processing GL commands on the CPU. Reduce this by minimizing the number of GL calls you make, particularly the number of state changes you make. Run your app with OpenGL ES Analyzer in Instruments for more advice on how to improve how your application calls OpenGL ES.

DYGLERSimplifyAlgorithm.target: Use a simpler algorithm. For example, use textures as lookup tables to replace complex functions.

DYGLEFRUseShortIndices.target: Use 16-bit (GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT) instead of 8-bit (GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE) vertex indices for greater efficiency. GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT is the smallest native size for vertex indices on iOS devices.

DYGLEFRTilingLimited.target: Performance is limited by the tiling processor of the GPU. Tiling processes the triangles you submit splitting them across tiles before processing each tile in turn.

DYGLERGLLimited.target: Frame rate of your app is limited by the graphics pipeline

DYGLEFRFBColorWriteLimited.target: Performance is limited by the number of color writes to the frame buffer. Use less blend operations to reduce the number of color writes.

DYGLEFRTextureFilterLimited.target: Performance is limited by performing filtering on texture reads in a fragment shader. Use mipmapped bilinear (GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_NEAREST) for the minify filter for the best balance of filtering performance and image quality.
